question: On 26 January the Venezuelan Supreme Court of Justice confirmed the disqualification from running for president of María Corina Machado and other opposition leaders from holding public office in the country, making clear the regime’s intentions not to allow the holding of fair, free and transparent presidential elections when Venezuleans are next called on to vote, elections that would set the country back on the road to democracy.

These events hinder the dialogue, promoted by the Union and other international stakeholders, which was taking place in Barbados between the Unitary Platform and the regime of Nicolás Maduro to reach an agreement to put an end to the political crisis in the country. 1.

Given that these actions violate the social and political rights of the illegally disqualified candidates and undermine democracy and the rule of law in Venezuela, will the VicePresident/High Representative urge the Council to include the new President of the Supreme Court of Justice, Caryslia Beatriz Rodríguez, on the list of persons sanctioned by the Union?

With this in mind and taking into account the fact that the recommendations of the last EU Election Observation Mission to the regional and municipal elections in Venezuela in 2021 have not been implemented, is the EEAS considering sending an Election Observation Mission for the upcoming presidential elections in the country?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (14.3.2024) The European Union has expressed publicly1 its deep concern about recent developments in Venezuela, including the Supreme Court’s ratification of the disqualification of María Corina Machado and other opposition leaders from the upcoming presidential elections.

Decisions intended to prevent members of the opposition from exercising their core political rights can only undermine democracy and rule of law. The EU restrictive measures are a means to encourage the restoration of democracy, the rule of law and respect for human rights in Venezuela. These measures can be scaled or reversed depending on the evolution of the situation.
Any decision on this matter needs to be taken unanimously by Member States in the Council. The EU continues supporting Venezuelan-led negotiations that can lead to more democratic elections.

Regarding an Election Observation Mission, the EU will consider any formal request by the authorities of Venezuela, taking into account the situation in the country, including the participation of the opposition in the elections and other elements relevant for an electoral observation.
